articles.title: El Barcelona ya ha encontrado a su '9'
articles.standfirst: Sportium sitúa a Raphinha como el gran rival de Mbappé en la lucha por el 'Pichichi' de LaLiga
articles.summary: Sportium sitúa a Raphinha como el gran rival de Mbappé en la lucha por el 'Pichichi' de LaLiga
articles.body: El Barcelona lleva todo el verano peleando por el fichaje de Julián Álvarez... pero todo parece indicar que el delantero argentino se quedará en el Atlético de Madrid. El club azulgrana trabaja en algún movimiento de última hora para incorporar otro ariete que ayude a cubrir las salidas de Lewandowski y Ferran. Flick, sin embargo, parece haber encontrado en Raphinha a su nuevo '9' en caso de emergencia. Una decisión que está teniendo impacto en las apuestas deportivas. Flick, desde luego, le ha cambiado la vida a Raphinha en el Barcelona. Cuando llegó el técnico alemán, el brasileño tenía colgado el cartel de transferible... pero terminó convirtiéndose en el jugador que mejor representa su estilo. Marcó 34 goles en su primera temporada a sus órdenes y la pasada, aun teniendo bastantes lesiones, llegó hasta los 21. Sin duda, los mejores años de su carrera. Acostumbrado a partir como extremo por la banda izquierda, Flick lo ubicó como delantero en el estreno liguero contra el Elche. La prueba salió a pedir de boca: Raphinha marcó dos goles y repartió una asistencia, convirtiéndose en uno de los grandes protagonistas de la goleada azulgrana. Todo apunta a que tendrá continuidad en esta nueva posición y Sportium ya ha tomado nota. De hecho, sitúa a Raphinha como el gran rival de Mbappé en la lucha por el 'Pichichi' de LaLiga. El brasileño cuenta con una cuota de 9.0 para terminar la temporada como máximo goleador, todavía bastante por detrás del delantero del Real Madrid, pero ya por delante de buena parte de los grandes candidatos al premio. Las mejores casas de apuestas así comienzan a reflejar el impacto que puede tener el cambio de posición del brasileño durante toda la temporada. Al Barcelona le toca recibir esta semana al Athletic Club en el Camp Nou, una prueba de mayor exigencia para comprobar si Raphinha mantiene su nueva posición de referencia ofensiva. El brasileño, además, tiene buenos antecedentes ante el conjunto dirigido por Edin Terzic, al que ha marcado tres goles en los ocho partidos que ha disputado frente a ellos. Sportium paga a 2.15 que vuelva a ver portería en este próximo encuentro.

articles.title: Fantasy Football: Justin Boone's backup running back rankings for 2026
articles.summary: It's key to know which understudies could take off in fantasy football.
articles.body:
Every fantasy football manager knows how quickly things can change when it comes to one of the most physical positions in football: running back. Staying prepared and knowing which backs are next in line for touches will always give you an edge on the competition.

It's also important to understand which backups have a chance to rise the depth chart based on talent, which ones are poised for a leading role when injuries strike and those who would max out as part of a less appealing replacement committee.

Here's how I'm ranking the top backup running backs based on their fantasy potential in 2026.

While I believe it's only a matter of time before Henderson emerges as the lead back in New England , it's clear he'll once again start the season behind Rhamondre Stevenson . The goal with my work is always to project how the next campaign will look and get ahead of how backfields will develop, but Henderson still has work to do in order to prove he deserves the top spot on the depth chart.

The coaching staff has made it clear they need to see more from him as a pass protector and between-the-tackles runner. So far, it doesn't sound like Henderson has answered the call in that area this summer.

The 23-year-old (turns 24 in October) is also dealing with a new lower ankle injury , after slipping on the turf during practice. He's walking and moving fine, but will undergo precautionary tests.

We'll see if this injury finally pushes Henderson's ADP below Stevenson's, which is how I've had it ranked for a while now. At the moment, Henderson is being taken in Round 6 as the RB26, while Stevenson is going off the board as the RB28 in the seventh round.

Henderson is still holding down the No. 1 spot based on his performance as a rookie, which resulted in 911 rushing yards, 221 receiving yards and 10 total TDs. A good chunk of that production came over the final eight weeks when Henderson took advantage of Stevenson being banged up and posted top-10 numbers at the position during that stretch. He flashed more than enough potential to think he can grow into a bigger role and become a weekly fantasy difference-maker.

In the meantime, Stevenson will begin the season offering RB3 fantasy production with Henderson being more of a boom-or-bust weekly RB3 with massive upside when the balance of the backfield shifts. We just don't know if that will occur this year or not.

Brooks is finally making headlines for the right reasons, after spending the first two seasons of his career recovering from ACL tears. The former second-round pick is back on the practice field and reminding fantasy managers what he's capable of when healthy. The 22-year-old even earned some praise from head coach Dave Canales recently.

Current starter Chuba Hubbard had a down year due to injuries, but he's just one season removed from a 1,366-yard, 11-touchdown campaign that allowed him to finish as the RB12 in fantasy points per game. The veteran still has some tread on his tires entering his age-27 season, but he's sat out most of August with a hamstring injury that's expected to keep him sidelined until Week 1.

Whether he maintains the lead back job will depend on his health, as well as Brooks' ability to return to his pre-injury form.

Fantasy managers searching for the next breakout or sleeper will be eyeing Brooks — and for good reason, since we've seen this backfield produce for fantasy at various stretches over the last couple seasons under Canales.

Brooks is one of the few players on this list who could take over the starting role without needing an injury ahead of him on the depth chart. Though his ADP is rising, he should be considered a high-ceiling stash and potential flex option, who has a realistic shot to become the lead back in Carolina before the end of the season.

There aren't many running backs who can brag that they posted over 1,300 scrimmage yards each of the past two seasons, but Dowdle is one of them. He accomplished the feat in 2024 with the Cowboys and again last season with the Panthers, when he overtook an injured Chuba Hubbard and erupted with a pair of 200-yard games before eventually cooling off down the stretch.

Now, he's reunited with his former head coach Mike McCarthy in Pittsburgh , who knows him well from their time together in Dallas . That could result in Dowdle capturing a significant role in the Steelers ' offense and perhaps even overtaking Jaylen Warren as the lead back at some point.

For now, Warren and Dowdle seem poised to split touches 50-50 in a timeshare that looks like it could be a frustrating one for fantasy, because it has the potential to shift in either direction on a weekly basis. That ambiguity makes Dowdle an interesting fantasy pick though, since we've already seen him rise to the top of uncertain backfields in recent years.

Even if he remains behind Warren, Dowdle will have a chance to offer fantasy RB3 production while holding serious one-injury-away upside.

Corum took a major step forward in Year 2, earning a larger role behind Kyren Williams and ultimately finishing with 782 scrimmage yards and six touchdowns.

His best production came in the second half of the season, when he topped 50 yards in seven of his last 10 outings, including 81 yards and a touchdown in Week 13, 131 yards and two TDs in Week 14, 71 yards and a score in Week 15 and 61 yards and a TD in Week 16.

Even so, Williams has finished as a top-10 fantasy back on a per game basis for three straight campaigns and will continue to have the edge this season. It's also worth noting that Williams and Corum will both turn 26 later this year, so this isn't a situation where the younger back is coming for an older back's spot.

That all boils down to Williams being a fantasy RB2 while Corum is an RB3 with enticing upside in favorable game scripts.

Corum also carries more fantasy value thanks to being the No. 2 back in a Sean McVay system that tends to turn any starter into a quality fantasy option. Bottom line, Corum is one injury away from being a top-12 fantasy back.

The Bears were one of the backfields that could have been hit hard by an addition this offseason, but that move never materialized. That leaves D'Andre Swift as the lead back with Monangai as a very strong backup once he's healthy.

Monangai is currently sitting out with a hyperextended knee that could keep him on the sidelines in Week 1. Whenever he returns, he'll slide back into the complementary role behind Swift.

It took a month for Monangai to make his presence felt last year, but like most rookies, he did his best work after the bye. From Week 6 on, Monangai was the RB26 in fantasy points per game and finished the season with 947 scrimmage yards and five touchdowns.

Those numbers are even more impressive when you realize that Swift was the RB10 during that same span and ended the year with 1,386 yards and 10 touchdowns of his own. The 60-40 split is likely to continue and, given how well Ben Johnson's rushing attack has performed, Monangai will offer weekly fantasy RB3 results in the No. 2 spot.

Just don't forget what happened in the lone game Swift was sidelined. In that contest, Monangai capitalized on a soft Bengals' defense and poured in 176 rushing yards and 22 receiving yards. So there's a serious ceiling waiting to be unlocked if Swift were forced to sit out at any point.

The Vikings almost moved on from Aaron Jones Sr. before a last-minute contract revision kept him in Minnesota . However, the veteran back will turn 32 in December and comes with an extensive injury history, including 11 missed games over the last three seasons.

While Mason hasn't officially pushed his way past Jones on the depth chart, he's expected to handle more work this year as the team emphasizes an outside-zone scheme. Mason performed well in that type of rushing attack during his time with the 49ers.

The 27-year-old has also been productive in his opportunities with the Vikings. Despite the struggles of the offense as a whole, Mason was the RB16 in fppg when Jones was out of the lineup for over a month early last season (Week 3 to Week 7).

And when Jones sat out Week 18, Mason had his second-highest yardage total of the season with 94 yards on 14 carries. With Kyler Murray 's arrival hopefully breathing life into the offense, Mason could be a sneaky RB3/flex who might emerge as Minnesota 's lead back if Jones hits the trainer's table again.

Just note that sixth-round rookie Demond Claiborne could factor into the mix as a lightning fast big-play threat, who would pair well with Mason. If Claiborne is up to the task, it would lower any potential fantasy ceiling Mason offered.

Gainwell didn't find a starting job in free agency, but he came away with the next best thing. In Tampa Bay, he'll step into Rachaad White 's old role as an overqualified No. 2 back with weekly RB3/flex potential thanks to his pass-catching prowess.

Last year in Pittsburgh, Gainwell caught 73 balls for 486 yards and three touchdowns, while finishing the year with over 1,000 scrimmage yards and eight total TDs.

He also proved to be more than capable of handling the starting job when called upon. In the four games where Gainwell saw at least 15 touches for the Steelers, he posted 134 yards and two TDs in the first, 105 yards in the second, 122 yards in the third and 126 yards in the fourth. If Irving ever misses time again, Gainwell will immediately be in the conversation as a top-15 fantasy back.

All of a sudden the Broncos ' backfield seems crowded. J.K. Dobbins has returned and will likely begin the season as the starter once again, but like every other campaign in his career, an injury seems inevitable. Prior to the draft, that put Harvey in a similar situation to last season, when he was RB9 on a per game basis (15.3 fppg) from Week 11 on, with four top-12 weekly finishes over his last six outings.

However, Denver drafted Jonah Coleman in the fourth round, which complicates Harvey's outlook. He no longer has the same one-injury away upside, since Coleman would likely step into Dobbins' spot if the veteran missed time. That doesn't mean Harvey isn't valuable for fantasy. As a rookie playing in a part-time role alongside Dobbins, Harvey was the RB33 (8.7 fppg) and a boom-or-bust flex option before the veteran got hurt. Just understand that Harvey would need multiple injuries to occur around him in order to unlock the top-10 fantasy ceiling we saw from him down the stretch last year.

The competition in the Jaguars' backfield between 23-year-old Bhayshul Tuten and the 27-year-old Rodriguez has ramped up with Rodriguez back on the field after dealing with a foot injury that kept him sidelined during OTAs.

I still have my doubts about Rodriguez's fantasy ceiling, due to his limited pass-catching skills and uninspiring production over the first three seasons (held under 500 rushing yards every year). However, Rodriguez is a dependable option who head coach Liam Coen has an affinity for, going back to their time together when he served as his offensive coordinator at Kentucky.

Even if Tuten fails to emerge as a true lead back, Rodriguez would find himself in a committee with a fantasy ceiling as a low-end RB2/high-end RB3.

It's worth noting that last season, Tuten had over 100 touches and starter Travis Etienne Jr. was still a top-10 fantasy back on a per game basis. So Rodriguez should have a sizable role, while also providing his managers with one-injury-away upside in a very strong offense.

Though White has never been able to secure a full-time starting job in the NFL, he's a very capable pass-catcher who has excelled as a short-term starter when injuries required it.

From Week 5 to Week 12, White played over 55% of the Buccaneers' snaps while Bucky Irving was recovering from an injury. During that stretch, White was the RB24 in fppg.

In Washington, he'll have a clear role as the passing-down back while also battling for touches with Jacory Croskey-Merritt . In that scenario, White can be an RB3/flex in half PPR, with one-injury away upside. If JCM can't prove he's worthy of the starting role, White's volume will increase to the point where he could be a weekly RB2 option — while facing the sixth easiest schedule for fantasy backs.

articles.title: PMs são condenados por tortura de torcedor espancado em estádio | G1
articles.standfirst: Caso ocorreu em maio de 2022, após jogo entre São José e Brasil de Pelotas. Rai Duarte ficou em coma, passou mais de 100 dias internado e precisou passar por 14 cirurgias.
articles.summary: Caso ocorreu em maio de 2022, após jogo entre São José e Brasil de Pelotas. Rai Duarte ficou em coma, passou mais de 100 dias internado e precisou passar por 14 cirurgias.
articles.body:
Rai Duarte, torcedor do Brasil de Pelotas agredido por policiais militares em maio de 2022 — Foto: André Ávila/Agência RBS

A Justiça Militar condenou quatro policiais militares pelo crime de tortura contra o torcedor Rai Duarte , que ficou em coma após ser agredido durante uma abordagem da Brigada Militar (BM) em maio de 2022 , depois de uma partida de futebol.

O episódio ocorreu em 1º de maio de 2022, após jogo entre Brasil de Pelotas e São José, válido pela Série C do Campeonato Brasileiro, no Estádio Passo D'Areia, sede do clube de Porto Alegre .

Os condenados são os soldados Leandro Duarte Lemes, João Carlos Krauze e Kelli Lisiane Abreu Marques e o tenente Dilnei Leon , que comandava a equipe policial naquele dia. As penas variam de três a oito anos de reclusão.

O soldado Leandro Duarte Lemes foi condenado a 8 anos e 2 meses de prisão, em regime fechado.

O tenente Dilnei Silva Leon foi condenado a 7 anos e 2 meses de pena, a ser cumprida em regime semiaberto.

Os soldados João Carlos Krauze do Nascimento e Kelli Lisiane Abreu Marques foram condenados a 3 anos e 6 meses de reclusão, em regime aberto.

Todos vão recorrer da sentença em liberdade. O advogado Fábio César Silveira, que representa Leon e Krauze, afirma que "a decisão contraria o contexto probatório dos autos" e que vai recorrer. A advogada Ana Carolina Stein, que representa Lemes, também afirma que "a decisão não reflete o conjunto probatório dos autos” e que recorrerá da decisão. A reportagem busca contato com Kelli Lisiane Abreu Marques, advogada de Andrea Ferrari, mas ainda não obteve retorno.

Além das quatro condenações, outros 13 policiais militares que respondiam ao processo foram absolvidos.

O advogado de Rai Duarte informou que pretende recorrer da decisão . Segundo a manifestação citada pela reportagem, a defesa recebeu com tranquilidade a condenação dos quatro policiais, mas entende que os agentes absolvidos também tiveram participação no caso.

Segundo o julgamento, Rai foi retirado de um ônibus da torcida após uma confusão registrada depois da partida . Conforme a decisão judicial, ele não teria participado da briga , mas foi retirado do veículo mesmo assim. De acordo com a condenação, o torcedor foi levado para um banheiro e espancado pelos policiais .

Rai Duarte ficou em coma após as agressões, passou 116 dias hospitalizado e foi submetido a 14 cirurgias.

Em entrevista à RBS TV em julho, ainda internado, o torcedor alegou ter sido levado para dentro de uma sala e "agredido covardemente por 5 ou 6 policiais" : "Me agrediram, me jogaram no chão e depois me levaram para o hospital", disse.

Rai Duarte é agente de saúde em Pelotas e torcedor do Grêmio Esportivo Brasil. Ele foi internado em estado grave na noite de 1º de maio, após a partida entre Brasil e São José, no Estádio Passo D'Areia, em Porto Alegre.

Por volta das 19h, agentes do 11º BPM ingressaram no local para controlar uma briga. Após a confusão, quando torcedores do time visitante retornavam para a arquibancada, 11 deles foram encurralados pelos policiais , segundo a denúncia.

Rai Duarte, que não tinha participado do conflito , estava em um ônibus para voltar a Pelotas, quando foi retirado do veículo e preso por três policiais por motivo não esclarecido , conforme os promotores. Algemado, ele foi levado junto aos demais torcedores, sendo agredido em um banheiro .

O MP aponta que Rai sofreu lesões de natureza grave , como hemorragia intra-abdominal, ruptura de artéria cólica média, hematoma em mesocólon transverso, isquemia de cólon transverso, choque hemorrágico e escoriação no segundo dedo da mão esquerda.

De acordo com a denúncia, Rai teria questionado os policiais por não terem indicado o motivo da prisão . O torcedor, que foi policial militar temporário, também teria afirmado reconhecer os procedimentos, questionando a ação dos agressores.

Os PMs teriam conferido a identidade de Rai e, constatando que ele não seria um militar da ativa, passaram a agredir o torcedor com tapas, socos e chutes . Além disso, teriam proferido ofensas ao homem.

A acusação ainda afirma que os 12 torcedores sofreram agressões por mais de 40 minutos, sempre algemados, deitados ou sentados e não oferecendo resistência ou risco aos policiais.

O MP sustenta que os 17 policiais militares diziam estar acostumados a agredir torcedores do Brasil sempre que eles estivessem em Porto Alegre. Os agressores também teriam ameaçado "enxertar" drogas para incriminar os torcedores. Outra ameaça apurada foi que, caso as agressões fossem denunciadas, haveria represália.

Rai foi levado para um hospital. Imagens mostram o torcedor chegando ao local caminhando. Depois de um tempo dentro de uma sala, no entanto, ele é transportado em uma cadeira de rodas, já desacordado, para outro local . Segundo Rai, ao entrar no espaço, ele já estava com uma hemorragia interna, não suportou as dores e acabou desmaiando.

No inquérito policial militar feito pela BM, 10 PMs haviam sido indiciados por tortura e lesão corporal de natureza grave , enquanto outro agente foi responsabilizado por tortura e tentativa de homicídio . Os demais envolvidos teriam participado com nível menor de comprometimento , segundo a corporação.

articles.title: Van Oevelen: “Dimitrievski es un gran portero, depende de mí mostrar al entrenador de lo que soy capaz”
articles.standfirst: Presentación oficial del guardameta neerlandés, que estuvo en el banquillo en el partido ante el Betis
articles.summary: Presentación oficial del guardameta neerlandés, que estuvo en el banquillo en el partido ante el Betis
articles.body: El Valencia presentó oficialmente este miércoles al guardameta neerlandés Kayne Van Oevelen, una incorporación que llega para reforzar la portería valencianista tras un verano marcado por los cambios en su futuro. El portero, que finalmente desembarca en Mestalla cedido por el Ipswich Town después de que el interés del Valencia surgiera meses atrás, se mostró ilusionado por vestir la camiseta blanquinegra y agradecido por la confianza recibida desde su llegada. En el acto, Andrés Palop fue el encargado de darle la bienvenida a través de un vídeo: “Mestalla y su afición son muy exigentes, estoy seguro de que vas a ayudar al equipo a conseguir sus objetivos”. Van Oevelen aseguró que afronta esta etapa con ambición, dispuesto a trabajar para ganarse oportunidades, aprender de Stole Dimitrievski y demostrar sus cualidades bajo palos. Además, destacó el ambiente de Mestalla, al que calificó de "increíble", y reconoció que llegar al Valencia era el objetivo que perseguía desde tiempo atrás. ¿Cómo fue su verano porque el Valencia lo quiso inicialmente y al final llega procedente del Ipswich Town cedido?: “Ha sido un verano muy raro y largo. Pero estoy contento de estar aquí. Efectivamente fue el Ipswich Town el club que me firmó, pero estoy muy feliz de estar aquí en el Valencia”. ¿Cómo le ha convencido el proyecto del Valencia sabiendo que quizá no vaya a tener muchos minutos aquí?: “Tuve varias reuniones con el entrenador de porteros, su actitud fue muy positiva, también los compañeros, los jugadores y ahora llega mi turno de demostrarlo, trabajar duro y darlo todo”. Cómo es como portero: “Me gusta trabajar duro también animo a mis compañeros desde atrás, soy un portero que me considero bueno con los pies, también voy bien por alto y en la salida de balón. Así es más o menos como me veo”. ¿Le han dicho que rol va a tener en el Valencia?: “Dimitrievski es un gran portero, todos lo pueden ver. Depende de mí empujarme a mí y enseñar al entrenador de lo que soy capaz” ¿Es un paso circunstancial el Valencia o cree que podría quedarse más tiempo? “No sé lo que pasará en el futuro. Lo veremos”. ¿Cree que puede ser titular en algún momento de la temporada? “Depende del futuro, no lo puedo saber. Voy a dar lo mejor para ser titular, empujarme a mí mismo y a él también, aprendiendo de él también para mejorar en el futuro”. ¿Cómo valora el ambiente en Mestalla?: “El estadio es increíble, de un gran club y también el ambiente de los aficionados. Mucho ruido, cosa que me gustó. Es normal que cuando se escapan puntos haya este tipo de reacciones y nosotros estamos aquí para trabajar y empezar a mejorar a partir del próximo domingo”. ¿Por qué sale de Ipswich Town al mes de ficharlo? “Tenía que demostrarme a mí mismo que puedo trabajar duro, era decisión de Ipswich y me alegro de la decisión que tomó, me alegra estar aquí en el Valencia”. Sale de la Eredivisie para ir a la Premier, pero finalmente recala en la Liga, ¿cómo ve la competición? "Esta Liga tiene más calidad, los jugadores, los equipos. En el modo de jugar diría que es similar, parecido, pero destacaría la calidad de los jugadores". ¿Está donde quería estar en el mes de julio? “Sí. Es el motivo por el que estoy aquí ahora. Y estoy feliz, es un honor defender este escudo y esta camiseta”.

articles.title: Elijah Gift, muy cerca del Eibar
articles.standfirst: El extremo rojiblanco llegará cedido; Aranbarri le conoce bien porque le entrenó el pasado curso en el Bilbao Athletic
articles.summary: El extremo rojiblanco llegará cedido; Aranbarri le conoce bien porque le entrenó el pasado curso en el Bilbao Athletic
articles.body: Elijah Gift será la guinda del mercado del Eibar. El conjunto armero negocia con el Athletic la cesión del extremo de 20 años, que ha estado a las órdenes de Edin Terzic durante la pretemporada. La idea inicial en Ibaigane era que el futbolista formara parte del día a día del primer equipo y compitiera con el Bilbao Athletic, pero el interés eibartarra ha cambiado los planes del Athletic. La apuesta del Eibar por Gift responde a la confianza que tiene en él Jokin Aranbarri, que conoce a la perfección sus virtudes porque le tuvo a sus órdenes la pasada temporada en el filial rojiblanco. El jugador formado en el Liverpool es un extremo explosivo, vertical y con desborde. Tres cualidades fundamentales para Aranbarri en las bandas. Con el técnico guipuzcoano disputó 30 partidos en los que hizo dos goles en el año de su debut en Primera Federación. Gift es un jugador cuyo fichaje por el Athletic despertó mucha expectación. El club bilbaíno desembolsó un millón al Liverpool para hacerse con sus servicios cuando tenía 17 años. Nacido en la localidad navarra de Corella, Mikel González no dudó en poner su mirada en el habilidoso extremo. Se trataba de una apuesta a largo plazo que sigue quemando etapas y ahora está a punto de vivir su primera aventura como profesional en Ipurua En la cesión de Gift no se contempla ninguna opción de compra y las condiciones del préstamo pueden variar en función del protagonismo que tenga un futbolista que no llega a Ipurua para ser titular, pero que puede desempeñar un papel importante como revulsivo en las segundas mitades por su capacidad para ser vertical y profundo. El acuerdo está a punto de cerrarse y en los próximos días podría oficializarse la que sería sexta incorporación veraniega del Eibar, que se mantiene expectante al desenlace final del mercado con la misión de no perder a ninguna pieza importante. El futuro de Jonmi Magunagoitia no parece peligrar y el objetivo es que el de Gift sea el último movimiento armero

articles.title: El Deportivo abrirá una mesa de diálogo con la federación de peñas
articles.standfirst: Para intentar reconducir la situación con los aficionados
articles.summary: Para intentar reconducir la situación con los aficionados
articles.body: El Deportivo anunció esta mañana que su intención es abrir una mesa de diálogo con representantes de las peñas y con miembros de Marathon inferior. José Manuel García, director de Medios del club, comenzó esta mañana en la rueda de prensa ofrecidas por el Dépor, haciendo alusión al problema social que tienen. “Tenemos una situación social que nos preocupa y ocupa, son cosas que no somos ajenos a ellas y queremos tomar las riendas de esto de forma responsable para encontrar una potencial solución”. Desde el Deportivo quieren enderezar una situación que se está complicando cada día más. “La afición es un pilar fundamental, no el único, pero sí fundamental. Los pilares son; lo social, el proyecto de infraestructuras, la parte financiera, corporativa y la deportiva, la más visible. Todos estos pilares solo funcionan si son un engranaje, sin un pilar puede girar igual, pero va a ser más complicado. Queremos que todos los pilares encajen como un engranaje”, expresó. También estuvieron presentes en la rueda de prensa Jesús Blanco, director de seguridad y Santiago Liste, responsable del departamento jurídico. articles.title: Joan Laporta: "Seguimos muy interesados en Julián Alvarez"
articles.standfirst: El presidente valora la situación del mercado culé y la actualidad azulgrana
articles.summary: El presidente valora la situación del mercado culé y la actualidad azulgrana
articles.body: Joan Laporta valoró este miércoles el estado del mercado azulgrana, que tiene a Julián Álvarez como protagonista principal, y los principales temas de actualidad culé. El presidente catalán hizo una declaración institucional en la que, entre otras cosas, afirmó que mantienen intacto su interés en el delantero del Atlético. No tiran la toalla por él, porque el internacional albiceleste quiere jugar en el Barça y porque el conjunto rojiblanco está negociando con otros clubs para traspasarlo. “Que sepan que, si están dispuestos a vender al jugador durante esta ventana de transferencias de verano, estaríamos listos para comprarlo, siempre y cuando podamos llegar a un acuerdo en torno a la oferta que les hemos hecho”, explicó Laporta en su discurso. El mensaje al Atlético, fue directo: el Barça mantiene su intención de firmar a Julián Álvarez, pero sin estar dispuesto a abonar los 500 millones de su cláusula de rescisión. La propuesta presentada era de 100. “Seguimos muy interesados en Julián Álvarez. Nos gustaría que aceptaran nuestra oferta, y lo estamos haciendo con el máximo respeto hacia el Atlético de Madrid. Nos gustaría entendernos”, añadió el mandatario culé, mostrándose conciliador aunque firme en su intención de firmar al delantero argentino. Laporta explicó cómo fue y cómo está siendo todo el proceso de negociación. "Quiero decir que tenemos un gran respeto por el Atlético de Madrid y sus dirigentes. Hace muchos años que nos conocemos. Quiero explicar cómo fue. Hicimos una oferta de club a club. Esta oferta yo la ratifiqué en una conversación telefónica personal con Miguel Ángel Gil. Ellos me dijeron que no tenían intención de vender porque no tenían alternativa a Julián y le dije que a nosotros nos interesaba, pero que respetábamos que no quisieran vender, aunque si encontraban una alternativa dentro de este mercado, nosotros estábamos con interés de hacer el fichaje", comentó en su discurso. El mandatario catalán explicó que el interés se mantiene ante las informaciones que apuntan que el conjunto rojiblanco está en conversaciones con el Arsenal por el internacional albiceleste: "Pensamos con Deco que, viendo que no lo vendían, dejábamos el tema en stand by. ¿Qué ha pasado? Nos han llegado informaciones de que el Atlético de Madrid está negociando con otros clubes por el futbolista. Nosotros seguimos presentes con nuestra oferta porque es vox populi que el jugador quiere venir al Barça. Esta situación ha creado mucho ruido, que no es motivado por acciones del Barça. Hablamos con Enrique Cerezo y luego él habló. Yo a él lo aprecio mucho y quiero decir que el Barça ha estado a la altura de las circunstancias. Hemos hecho lo mismo que hacemos con otros clubes. Nosotros continuamos presentes y la oferta es vigente. Sigue en caso de que el Atlético quiera vender al jugador". El Barcelona tiene claro que Julián Álvarez es la única opción para reforzar su ataque este verano, no firmará a ningún otro jugador, y el mensaje de Laporta es un espaldarazo al delantero rojiblanco, que vive una situación muy complicada en el Atlético. "Parece ser que el jugador quiere venir al Barça, por lo tanto, nosotros mantenemos nuestra ilusión, nuestra intención, con todos los respetos para el Atlético de Madrid, de poder fichar al jugador", comentó, satisfecho y esperanzado, Joan Laporta. "Mantenemos nuestra propuesta, nuestra oferta, y ojalá haya un entendimiento entre los dos clubs", concluyó el presidente del Barcelona.

articles.title: La carta con la que Gourlay trata de salvar 'su' mercado en el Valencia: un nombre
articles.standfirst: En su hoja de ruta ha estado presente la idea de traer una guinda de un jugador notorio en el último instante... si bien a cinco días del cierre hay demasiados frentes abiertos
articles.summary: En su hoja de ruta ha estado presente la idea de traer una guinda de un jugador notorio en el último instante... si bien a cinco días del cierre hay demasiados frentes abiertos
articles.body: El Valencia vive abocado a unos días intensos y repletos de nervios porque ahora sí que no se puede errar en una negociación. Si lo hace corre el riesgo de quedarse sin jugadores y sin capacidad de reacción. Básicamente por tiempo. El mercado cierra el próximo lunes a medianoche y la cuenta atrás ya ha comenzado. Pero el CEO del Valencia, Ron Gourlay, tiene su propia carta para intentar salvar una ventana que ha sido muy confusa en el mercado y donde el Valencia no ha perfilado con conocimiento de causa el mismo. El de dejar su particular 'buen sabor de boca' que maquille el resto. Todo por salvar su situación. El escocés está señalado públicamente por la presión que hay en el entorno. Pero en sus planes hay una forma de intentar cerrar este mercado siempre y cuando puedan darse las circunstancias económicas o de espacio en plantilla. Intentar cerrarlo con un jugador que tenga nombre. Y en ello está... si puede porque ahora mismo las necesidades son muchas para confeccionar una plantilla competitiva. Este fin busca 'recompensar' en cierto modo el sufrimiento que ha sido estos meses de gestión donde ha costado mucho llegar a buen puerto en las distintas operaciones, pero el CEO es de los que cree que un jugador con nombre puede ayudarle en el momento final del mismo. Porque agentes e intermediarios han estado ofreciendo jugadores conocidos para casos extremos como es el final de un mercado donde hay más opciones en condiciones cercanas al 'estilo Valencia' donde la inversión es mínima y ahí puede acogerse. La planificación que ha seguido es que si se da en el último momento una posibilidad 'ganga' de un jugador que no entra en los planes de un equipo importante, intentar traerlo a préstamo con lo que solamente hacer frente al pago de una parte de la ficha. Y en esas están. Porque las últimas semanas han ido llegando ofrecimientos que han hecho agentes e intermediarios de posibles jugadores con nombre. El plan del verano era cerrar jugadores en una primera fase que apenas costaran como así fue -casos De Haas o Dieng- pero el plan se fue abajo con la segunda fase, a mediados del mes de julio, en el momento en que el belga Meunier se les escapó por no firmar la operación con antelación. Ese fue el ocaso. El caos. El principio de todos los males porque se pretendía contar con la base para la pretemporada e ir introduciendo leves detalles al plantel de Corberán a lo largo de la segunda quincena de julio y todo agosto con el equipo casi ensamblado en la parcela de refuerzos. Pero todo se les truncó por las distintas formas que han tenido de verlo internamente las partes. Ese coste cero por no disponer de capital para invertir llevaba a jugadores sin tener que pagar traspaso, pero luego llegaba la palabra de Corberán que ha frenado muchos de ellos.

articles.title: Uefa set to call off World Cup boycott after failed Fifa sell-off plan
articles.summary: All 55 Uefa members threatened to boycott Fifa tournaments if Gianni Infantino’s much-criticised proposal went ahead
articles.body:
Uefa is set to call off its boycott of the World Cup and Fifa tournaments after Gianni Infantino 's doomed sell-off plan failed to materialise.

Last month, European football's governing body and all 55 members announced plans to boycott all Fifa-sanctioned tournaments until Infantino dropped his proposal to sell off stakes in Fifa tournaments – and when "assurances have been made that such attempts to disfigure the game in this way will never be made again."

Now, The Guardian reports that Uefa bosses will tell its executive committee and presidents of numerous of the 55 member associations at a meeting in Monaco on Thursday that those two conditions have been met.

Time is of the essence, too, with six European teams (including England) set to fly to Poland on Monday for the Fifa Under-20 Women's World Cup, which starts on Saturday 5 September.

It also removes any uncertainty surrounding the senior England women's football team, as they look to navigate play-offs later this year to qualify for next summer's World Cup in Brazil.

The Independent has approached Uefa for comment.

However, Uefa's position on Infantino's position as Fifa president has not changed – with numerous associations withdrawing their support for him ahead of next year's presidential election.

Infantino's position and Uefa's next steps will be discussed at said meeting on Thursday, which takes place before the Champions League league-stage draw at 5pm (BST) in Monte-Carlo.

Infantino is facing demands to step down from three major confederations, with Asia's AFC, and Concacaf, which governs football across North and Central America and the Caribbean, joining Uefa in opposition. The sport's regional ruling bodies have also held discussions regarding a potential vote of no confidence against the Fifa chief.

Serious concerns have also been raised over the inaugural Fifa peace prize awarded to US president Donald Trump in December, as well as the overturning of a ban for American forward Folarin Balogun during this year's World Cup after a call from Trump.

Meanwhile, European Leagues President Claudius Schaefer, who has called for fundamental structural reform within Fifa, insists Infantino has no future at the top of world football's governing body.

Speaking in an interview with The Athletic published on Wednesday, Schaefer expressed grave concerns regarding Infantino's leadership on behalf of European Leagues, an organisation representing 53 professional men's and women's football competitions.

"We question his suitability to continue as president. Here in Switzerland, we've had a close view of Fifa and it seems that the influence of the president has grown from year to year," he added.

"Major decisions are taken without meaningful consultation with stakeholders who will be affected."

articles.title: El Atlético explota: "La única víctima del caso Julián somos nosotros"
articles.standfirst: Indignación rojiblanca: "Se está victimizando al jugador, pero el daño económico y reputacional es para el club"
articles.summary: Indignación rojiblanca: "Se está victimizando al jugador, pero el daño económico y reputacional es para el club"
articles.body: Tajante. Así se manifiestan en el Atlético sobre el caso Julián. Tras meses de polémicas y enredos, la situación se ha enquistado. Sucedió el pasado domingo con la explosión de la grada ante el Villarreal. Ha vuelto a suceder hoy mismo, cuando el jugador ha comunicado que no acudía a entrenar por encontrarse indispuesto. Y el Atlético ha dicho basta a todo este enredo. De forma contundente: "Se está victimizando al jugador, pero la única víctima del caso Julián somos nosotros", deslizan varias fuentes autorizadas de un club cansado del proceder del agente del jugador, pero también de un Barcelona que lleva meses mareando al jugador. "Nos han perjudicado en lo económico y en lo social", insisten en el club para advertir de nuevo que todo este problema tiene como víctima principal a un Atlético que insiste en su postura: "Hay 0% de posibilidades de venderlo al Barça", como respuesta a la insistencia de que sea el Camp Nou el destino final. "Esta situación no va de dinero, va de dignidad", insisten desde el Metropolitano. "Se ha creado una campaña con muchas mentiras y medias verdades. El único que paga esto es el Atlético". Una afirmación para poner en valor que su gran estrella está fuera del rendimiento esperado como se vio ante el Villarreal en el reencuentro con su afición. Por eso desde el Atlético insisten que sólo hacen que defender los intereses de la institución. De ahí que la denuncia presentada en su día será actualizada con todo lo que están haciendo tanto los azulgrana como un Fernando Hidalgo que ha manejado los hilos desde hace meses para sacar al jugador. Hasta el punto de no aceptar la oferta de renovación de marzo que le convertía en el jugador mejor pagado (pasaba de 7 a 10 millones de euros) y a tampoco escuchar el plazo que le pusieron los que mandan en el club: una oferta de 150 millones de euros (sin comisiones) que tendría que haber llegado el 20 de junio... y que nunca acabó en los despachos de un Atlético que ha dicho basta en el caso Julián. Todo ello, claro, en un escenario médico en el que los rojiblancos respaldan al jugador, al que ayudarán cuando se encuentre bien pese a que no se entiende que se 'juegue' con temas tan delicados como la salud mental y cuadros de ansiedad o depresión. En el Atlético, en cualquier caso, ponen sus servicios médicos a la disposición del jugador para que se incorpore a la dinámica del equipo con garantías de estar bien.

articles.summary: The opening weekend has already given us plenty to think about, but there’s little time to dwell on those results as the Premier League moves into its second...
articles.body:
The opening weekend has already given us plenty to think about, but there's little time to dwell on those results as the Premier League moves into its second round of fixtures.

From Manchester City's trip to Selhurst Park and Spurs facing Newcastle to Arsenal heading to Villa Park, there are some intriguing games ahead.

Here are my predictions for the weekend.

I believe in sport success can be decided by the smallest details, so take into account what a massive moment the last few minutes at the Etihad on Sunday were for Maresca.

He was seconds away from a massive spotlight being on him all week. Instead, he got away with overcomplicating his team selection, and it will be interesting if he tries those tactics again.

Selhurst Park can be a tricky ground to go to, but maybe Friday night is a good time to get this fixture out of the way?

As I write this, it's not clear if Sarr is simply injured or has gone AWOL to force a move to Galatasaray.

With the tax laws, I can understand why Turkey appeals to many players, but surely the 28-year-old would have interest elsewhere in England.

It's also not ideal when your striker is trying to prove legally that the last year of his contract is invalid.

Mateta and Sarr leaving could be the difference between the Eagles battling relegation or not, although so could keeping two unhappy players.

Two new managers who are insisting it will take time for their respective squads to learn and be physically able to handle their ethos.

To paraphrase Oliver Glasner, he's adamant that after two defeats to Leeds , Forest cannot expect a quick fix, even though he saw signs that players were understanding his principles.

Someone needs to tell the Austrian it's not the fans at the City Ground he needs to convince to be patient; it's their owner.

As for Liverpool, quite simply, these are the kind of games at Anfield they were not winning last season.

The Cherries were so close to their first-ever win in the Prem at the Etihad.

Marco Rose will take plenty of positives from the game; his only disappointment will be that the goals they conceded were soft. It's not like Man City were knocking down the door.

Play like that on Saturday and the German will get his first points.

The best chance a promoted team has of avoiding relegation is getting points on the board early, so this is a golden opportunity for Hull.

If they didn't sit back against Man United , there would be no reason to think they will on Saturday.

Coventry are not going to let one bad night at the Emirates ruin their special day this weekend, hosting Premier League football for the first time since 2001.

Because of the manner of the Brentford defeat, it's already a massive game for De Zerbi.

Spurs continue to spend so much money yet started the campaign with the same old story.

You would feel sorry for their fanbase if they had been more humble during the summer. I have heard their supporters make some crazy predictions without a ball being kicked.

For nearly two years, their fans have pointed to injuries as the reason for consecutive 17th-place finishes.

Last Saturday, even their manager was saying physically his team wasn't ready because many either were not fit or had been at the World Cup.

Reminder: Tottenham chose to have their pre-season in New Zealand and Australia!!!!

Monday showed why Chelsea can challenge for the title but ultimately why they might not have enough to get over the line.

An attack of Palmer, Rodgers and Pedro might be as good as any in the division, meaning Arsenal are taking a gamble if they let Martinelli leave without a replacement lined up.

Unless they sign another defender or keeper, though, they won't have enough.

Both won their opening Premiership games last weekend as well as qualifying in the Carabao Cup.

Yet Leeds will defend a lot better than Spurs did. Daniel Farke has built a team who can stay in a game, be hard to break down and then be clinical.

A lot within the football community have suggested both these clubs could struggle to maintain the standards they set last campaign.

Fulham, though, ended last season without a win in their last 11 games, so I'm tempted to go for home advantage but will go for a draw.

The narrative over Michael Carrick always was that being full-time Man United manager was going to be trickier than being caretaker boss. They are almost two different jobs.

Starting the season against two newly promoted sides gave him a golden opportunity to fly out of the traps, but it also puts massive pressure on him if it goes wrong.

It already did at Hull, with the most worrying aspect being that too many of his players played like they thought they just had to show up.

After that experience, no excuse to take Sunday for granted.

Sport can be about timings and luck that you can't control, such as the calendar.

You'd rather this fixture be early in the season than a few months later when essentially a new squad has had a chance to settle.

That's not to say Monday will be easy; Unai Emery would be unlucky to ever concede goals again in the manner his side did at Brighton. Yet Martinez and Watkins were not even on the bench for Villa, meaning they are close to completely losing the spine of the team that lifted the Europa League.

articles.title: Worried about high school football safety? Here's what the stats show.
articles.summary: High school football is popular and fun. But after the tragic death of a 17-year-old Wisconsin football player, here are some facts to consider.
articles.body:
Wisconsin loves football. On Friday nights across the state, teenagers and parents pack bleachers to watch high school games. On Saturdays, attention turns to the college level. And Packer Sundays are a singular ritual.

What's become better understood this century is the danger, at all ages, of immediate and long-term neurological damage from football hits.

Alma Center Lincoln 17-year-old Adam Massman's death Aug. 22 after an injury during a high school football game was extremely rare. But it has elevated attention to the sport's potential for tragedy.

What should Wisconsin parents do with that information? If your child is going to play football, how can they stay safe?

Massman, a senior, got injured in a game Thursday, Aug. 20. A statement by the School District of Alma Center-Humbird-Merrillan didn't say what type of injury it was, but EMTs were at the game and Massman was taken to a hospital, where he later died.

Brianne Massman, Adam's mother, told the Journal Sentinel the family only knows for sure that Adam had helmet-to-helmet contact during the game.

"I mean, no one would ever think something that severe would really happen," she said in an Aug. 24 interview. "We're just completely devastated."

See photos of Alma Center Lincoln High School football player who died after game

How often do high school football players die?

Very rarely, and the number has decreased over the years. But it happens every year.

The National Center for Catastrophic Sports Injury Research compiles reports of football deaths and injuries at all age levels, in games, practices and workouts.

While it groups high school and middle school players together, its most recent annual report said there were five deaths in that age group in 2025. All five were classified as indirect, caused by exertional (like heat stroke) and medical reasons. There weren't any direct fatalities caused by traumatic injury.

From 2016 through 2025, there were an average of 8.4 deaths among middle- and high-schoolers per year – a total of 62 indirect and 22 direct.

The 22 direct fatalities were a 44% decrease from the previous 10 years, from 2006 through 2015, when there were 39.

The center found that the total number of direct traumatic injury-related deaths in football at all levels dropped 45% the past 10 years, compared to the previous 10 years.

How many youth football players suffer non-fatal injuries?

In 2025, there were 39 nonfatal "catastrophic" football injuries across all age levels, 31 of which occurred in middle- and high-school players, according to the center's 2026 report .

The center defines catastrophic football injuries as severe traumatic injuries, including brain and spinal cord injuries, skull and spinal fractures, and other injuries that result in permanent disability, temporary paralysis or other serious neurological outcomes.

What about long-term effects of repeated head injuries?

CTE, or chronic traumatic encephalopathy, is a progressive neurological disease caused by repeated hits to the head.

A recent New York Times story reported on a study that revealed one in four ex-NFL players who died over a recent six-year period had CTE. Scientists think the actual number is much higher because most former players don't have their brains examined upon death.

Can more non-contact football practices help?

There is a reason the Ivy League banned full-contact practices in 2016, and why the NCAA recommended one "live-contact" practice per week that same year. It's the same reason the NFL and the players' union have agreed to limit them, too.

Players practice far more often than they play games, and limiting full-contact practices is a way to reduce injuries, including to the head.

What else can a coach, player or family member do?

There's a common sports idiom to "rub some dirt on it," when describing how to handle a minor injury. It's shorthand for an old-school mentality of toughness.

From teaching proper tackling – head up, eyes on the ball, shoulders absorbing the hit – to seeking care immediately if an injury is suspected, make safety a priority.

What about flag football as an alternative?

If you're worried about your child being injured, there's a version of football that's less risky: Flag football.

A CDC study published in 2021 found football players – those who play the traditional game, with tackling – ages 6-14 sustained 15 times more head impacts than their flag football counterparts. Those playing tackle football also sustained 23 times more high-magnitude head impacts than those playing flag.

Youth tackle football players experienced a median of 378 head impacts during the season, while flag football players experienced a median of eight, according to the study.

Flag football's popularity is increasing across the country, for both girls and boys. In Wisconsin, interest in girls flag football is blossoming.

Jack Albright can be reached at JAlbright@usatodayco.com.

Alma Center Lincoln 17-year-old Adam Massman's death Aug. 22 after an injury during a high school football game was extremely rare. But it has elevated attention to the sport's potential for tragedy.

What should Wisconsin parents do with that information? If your child is going to play football, how can they stay safe?

Massman, a senior, got injured in a game Thursday, Aug. 20. A statement by the School District of Alma Center-Humbird-Merrillan didn't say what type of injury it was, but EMTs were at the game and Massman was taken to a hospital, where he later died.

Brianne Massman, Adam's mother, told the Journal Sentinel the family only knows for sure that Adam had helmet-to-helmet contact during the game.

"I mean, no one would ever think something that severe would really happen," she said in an Aug. 24 interview. "We're just completely devastated."

See photos of Alma Center Lincoln High School football player who died after game

How often do high school football players die?

Very rarely, and the number has decreased over the years. But it happens every year.

The National Center for Catastrophic Sports Injury Research compiles reports of football deaths and injuries at all age levels, in games, practices and workouts.

While it groups high school and middle school players together, its most recent annual report said there were five deaths in that age group in 2025. All five were classified as indirect, caused by exertional (like heat stroke) and medical reasons. There weren't any direct fatalities caused by traumatic injury.

From 2016 through 2025, there were an average of 8.4 deaths among middle- and high-schoolers per year – a total of 62 indirect and 22 direct.

The 22 direct fatalities were a 44% decrease from the previous 10 years, from 2006 through 2015, when there were 39.

The center found that the total number of direct traumatic injury-related deaths in football at all levels dropped 45% the past 10 years, compared to the previous 10 years.

How many youth football players suffer non-fatal injuries?

In 2025, there were 39 nonfatal "catastrophic" football injuries across all age levels, 31 of which occurred in middle- and high-school players, according to the center's 2026 report .

The center defines catastrophic football injuries as severe traumatic injuries, including brain and spinal cord injuries, skull and spinal fractures, and other injuries that result in permanent disability, temporary paralysis or other serious neurological outcomes.

What about long-term effects of repeated head injuries?

CTE, or chronic traumatic encephalopathy, is a progressive neurological disease caused by repeated hits to the head.

A recent New York Times story reported on a study that revealed one in four ex-NFL players who died over a recent six-year period had CTE. Scientists think the actual number is much higher because most former players don't have their brains examined upon death.

Can more non-contact football practices help?

There is a reason the Ivy League banned full-contact practices in 2016, and why the NCAA recommended one "live-contact" practice per week that same year. It's the same reason the NFL and the players' union have agreed to limit them, too.

Players practice far more often than they play games, and limiting full-contact practices is a way to reduce injuries, including to the head.

What else can a coach, player or family member do?

There's a common sports idiom to "rub some dirt on it," when describing how to handle a minor injury. It's shorthand for an old-school mentality of toughness.

From teaching proper tackling – head up, eyes on the ball, shoulders absorbing the hit – to seeking care immediately if an injury is suspected, make safety a priority.

What about flag football as an alternative?

If you're worried about your child being injured, there's a version of football that's less risky: Flag football.

A CDC study published in 2021 found football players – those who play the traditional game, with tackling – ages 6-14 sustained 15 times more head impacts than their flag football counterparts. Those playing tackle football also sustained 23 times more high-magnitude head impacts than those playing flag.

Youth tackle football players experienced a median of 378 head impacts during the season, while flag football players experienced a median of eight, according to the study.

Flag football's popularity is increasing across the country, for both girls and boys. In Wisconsin, interest in girls flag football is blossoming.

articles.title: Football Extra newsletter: Is there a looming problem for the Premier League?
articles.summary: How have Premier League spending rules influenced teams' behaviour this summer – and what do they mean for future competitive balance?
articles.body:
A curse of modern fandom is being required to understand the latest acronym that will dictate which way the wind blows your team for the foreseeable.

If you're outside the UK and would like to receive the Football Extra newsletter, head this way to sign up .

An awareness of these various mechanisms, like Uefa's Football Earnings guidelines, or the Premier League's Squad Cost Ratio (which replaced the Profit and Sustainability Rules this season), is of greater importance to some fanbases than others. Those who follow one of the 'big six' probably have to think about them a whole let less than supporters of a side like Aston Villa , Newcastle , Brighton or any of the other challenger teams seeking to gatecrash the elite.

The aim of this piece is not to describe what the rules now are – for a clear explanation on that, you can go here – but to analyse the impact of such regulations; how have they influenced teams' behaviour this summer – and what do they mean for the future competitive balance of the Premier League?

Villa Park provides the best case study in that at present. Unai Emery's side have performed miracles during the Spaniard's reign, qualifying for the Champions League twice, winning a European trophy and securing a top-seven league finish in each of his four full seasons.

"It's very hard to say they haven't done pretty much everything right from an execution perspective on the football side," Stefan Borson, football finance expert and head of sport at law firm McCarthy Denning, told BBC Sport. "I mean, somehow last season they even managed to qualify for the Champions League in two different routes. That's just unbelievable."

Yet for the past two summers the Villans have been operating under penalty from Uefa, having fallen foul of the European governing body's financial regulations during the 2024-25 season in which they returned to the Champions League.

As part of a settlement for breaching these cost controls, Villa agreed to reduce their spending fairly aggressively over a period of three years, to fall in line with Uefa's mandatory 70% squad cost limit. This means clubs in continental competition must not exceed spending that percentage of revenue on wages, transfers, and agent fees – much stricter than the 85% now permitted under the new Premier League rules.

Villa's business during this summer's window reflects how sharply that settlement continues to impact with several first-team players, including Ezri Konsa (to Arsenal ) and Morgan Rogers (to Chelsea ), departing for big fees. Meanwhile, Newcastle, Nottingham Forest and Chelsea have all received varying degrees of the same punishment for similar recent breaches.

But with the big six making more money than ever, supporters of aspiring clubs have questioned whether the convergence of European and domestic spending rules threatens to widen the chasm between the top earners and the chasing pack.

"It will compound that gap over time, largely because of the Champions League," Borson explained.

"Qualifying for that now is worth, let's say, £70million to £100m on average. If you can get that every year, that's such a massive advantage in terms of revenue and profit compared to the other teams, even after all the costs you incur from it.

"Villa have done it twice out of three years, which is an amazing achievement given their wage bill, but they did it by having to take the view that they would just breach Uefa's football earnings and SCR test. And because they've now breached that, then they have to restrict their spending. And so, to some extent, they're back to square one."

But if the only way to close the gap is to consistently qualify for the Champions League what choice is there but to spend, when the consequences of not qualifying for continental competition are so severe?

"Missing out on European football – particularly the Champions League now – is almost like a mini relegation," Borson added.

But there is another side of this debate. For every team in the restless middle class of the English top flight frustrated by the current regulatory landscape, there are others for whom this well-intended push for sustainability has come too late.

Teams like Bury, Macclesfield, Sheffield Wednesday – even Everton , who at one point seemed dangerously close to becoming the first top-flight team to enter administration since Portsmouth – have shown the clear need for some level of regulation, to protect clubs from themselves more than anything.

It is a "balancing act", said Dr Christina Philippou, an expert in sport finance at the University of Portsmouth, trying to facilitate ambition while "mitigating against your club disappearing forever".

"That [the club's existence being threatened] is a distinct possibility if it goes terribly," she continued. "The problem is ultimately ambition trumps everything until the unthinkable happens and then it's terrible. That's why the rules were introduced in the first place.

"But there have been so many tweaks over the years because every rule has side effect. It's like medicine. You take something for one thing, but it has a side effect. And for an illness that is really serious, people might take one set of medication to treat their disease and then another set to treat the side effects of their main medication. Tweaking the financial rules is very much like that.

"I don't think we've got to the perfect place yet. And I'm sure we will see more changes to the rules in the years to come."

In the meantime, those who want to bridge the gap are faced with the increasingly sobering reality that it just might not be possible.

"A team like Newcastle will generate a revenue of around £350m in the current season – £300m-£400m less revenue than the top Premier League teams in the Champions League," said Borson, "that means with the Premier League's 85% SCR limit, they may have a squad cost budget of £250m-£300m less than rivals.

"There is no one system that can cater for all clubs' particular preferences."

That cold, hard reality is one that supporters outside the big six are already coming to terms with – and one that, at least for now, means trends of the past few summers are likely to continue.

Carlos Baleba 's move from Brighton to Manchester United yesterday took spending from the big six on non-big six players to around £680m this summer, already eclipsing last year's figure. In total over the past two years, 25 players have left their clubs to join one of the elite half dozen compared to 37 in the eight seasons prior, marking a clear acceleration of this trend.

Within that context, it seems unlikely that challenger teams will ever be able to bridge the gap to their established rivals. To do so would mean sustaining their on-pitch success in defiance of teams with bigger resources, while selling their best players on to those same teams on almost annual basis.

Change may not be forthcoming though, as Philippou explained, it may be in the game's best interests to begin considering it.

"Competitive balance is really important to the health of the league long term," she said. "At some point people will wake up to that from a regulatory perspective and try to fix that side of things rather than just going 'well, it doesn't really matter'. Because it does matter for all clubs long term to have a healthy competition."

That points to an uncomfortable truth that underpins the whole debate: the rules exist to stop clubs destroying themselves, not to stop the strong getting stronger. Villa's punishment and Newcastle's revenue ceiling are proof the system works as designed – just perhaps not in the direction anyone outside the big six was hoping for.

Whether that's a problem regulators are willing to address may end up being the defining issue of the modern Premier League era.

articles.title: Barcelona double down on Julian Alvarez-or-nothing stance as deadline day approaches
articles.summary: With not long left until the summer transfer window slams shut, Barcelona have still not signed a new striker for Hansi Flick’s squad.The German manager has...
articles.body:
With not long left until the summer transfer window slams shut, Barcelona have still not signed a new striker for Hansi Flick's squad.

The German manager has shown that he is more than happy to experiment and play with Raphinha as the number nine, while Hamza Abdelkarim also offers an option.

Having scoured the market for alternatives, it was revealed yesterday that Barça had made a firm decision to stick with Alvarez as their only striker option in the market.

Now, according to journalist Florian Plettenberg , Alvarez remains the priority until deadline day, and the club are prepared to sign nobody if the Argentine cannot be secured.

Barça have explored other forwards, but the sporting department has now doubled down on Alvarez as the only target considered worth a major late investment.

Hansi Flick is said to be completely behind the pursuit.

The Barcelona coach views Alvarez as the forward he wants to complete the attack, while Deco is continuing to push and has no intention of giving up before the market closes.

The alignment between the director and the coach matters a lot in a long-drawn transfer saga such as this one.

Barça appear united internally over Alvarez, which explains why they are prepared to wait rather than panic-buy an alternative.

The financial side of the deal is said to be in place.

Barcelona will sign Julian Alvarez or no one. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images)

Joan Laporta has made the necessary funds available for Barcelona to complete the operation if Atletico Madrid finally agree to negotiate.

That means the biggest obstacle is no longer Barça 's willingness to spend. It is Atletico's stubborn decision not to negotiate with the Catalan club.

The Madrid club have consistently resisted the idea of selling Alvarez to Barcelona, despite the player's own preference and the growing tension around his situation.

Barça are willing to wait until the very end

Alvarez is having a very tough time at Atletico, where he has not looked his usual self and struggled to get going in the game against Villarreal .

He was booed intensely when his name was announced before the game and received a hostile reception when he was introduced during the match.

The relationship between the 26-year-old and the Atletico fans has been completely fractured, with seemingly no way back.

Laporta has publicly expressed interest in Alvarez. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images)

Barcelona president Joan Laporta revealed in an interview (h/t Fabrizio Romano ) that the club have information that Atletico are looking to sell the South American.

"We got the information that Atletico Madrid wants to sell the player," he said.

"It's clear that our offer remains valid until the end of the market."

However, even if Los Colchoneros make the decision to sell Alvarez this summer, there is no necessity for them to sell him to Barça .

The Catalans continue to push until the very end, but not much is going to change unless Los Colchoneros decide to relax their stance.

Barça have done what they can and assured the player that they will try to sign him until the very end of the window.

If they do not, the club appear prepared to walk away rather than settle for a second-choice striker, and it remains to be seen how that decision pans out.

articles.title: El Barça suspende el homenaje a los campeones del mundo y lo sustituye por un "acto de exaltación de la estelada"
articles.standfirst: Laporta transforma el evento en una jornada de protesta pacífica y defensa de la libertad de expresión tras las agresiones policiales a seguidores azulgranas en Elche
articles.summary: Laporta transforma el evento en una jornada de protesta pacífica y defensa de la libertad de expresión tras las agresiones policiales a seguidores azulgranas en Elche
articles.body: El Barcelona ha dado un giro a su estreno liguero en el Spotify Camp Nou. El conjunto culé ha decidido no rendir el homenaje a los campeones del mundo que se está haciendo en diferentes estadios de LaLiga y lo sustituirá por un "acto de exaltación de la estelada". "No es el contexto ni el momento más apropiado. El fútbol debe servir para unir y no para generar enfrentamientos que no convienen a nadie", comenta Laporta al respecto. En su lugar, la idea es realizar un "acto de exaltación de la estelada, que representa la forma de pensar de muchos culés y catalanes". El presidente del Barcelona añade: "Es una manera de expresarnos de forma pacífica que no genera violencia ni odio. Se debe respetar la estelada porque representa nuestros anhelos de libertad". El club volvió a condenar la actuación policial contra aficionados del Barça en la previas del partido ante el Elche. "Las imágenes son espeluznantes y muy claras. Una vez reconfirmados los hechos, pedimos que se apliquen las sanciones y los castigos pertinentes", señala el máximo mandatario del conjunto azulgrana, que cree que sacar la estelada ante el Athletic Club será un ejemplo de poder mostrar su opinión sin ver peligrar su identidad. "Que el acto sirva para que los culés y los catalanes podamos ir con la estelada sin que corra peligro nuestra integridad física y que este elemento deje de estar estigmatizado por las fuerzas de seguridad y orden público del Estado", dice Laporta, que además anunció que la entidad repartirá 10.000 esteladas en el exterior del estadio para llenar las gradas.

articles.title: García Macua: "¿Depende la supervivencia del club de 20 entradas para los expresidentes?"
articles.standfirst: El que fuera dirigente de 2007 a 2011 es crítico con algunas de las actuaciones de Uriarte
articles.summary: El que fuera dirigente de 2007 a 2011 es crítico con algunas de las actuaciones de Uriarte
articles.body: El arranque de la presente temporada ha llegado con recortes en la política de entradas de cortesía del club, que desde el partido ante el Atlético se pondrán a la venta. Muchas de ellas formarán parte de packs exclusivos, por lo que saldrán con precios mucho más elevados que el de una entrada al uso. La tijera ha sido amplia y salpica incluso hasta los expresidentes de la entidad, que actualmente son Lertxundi, Arrate, Ugartetxe, Lamikiz, Ana Urkijo, García Macua, Urrutia y Elizegi. La pasada campaña el club tuvo una reducción en butacas de palco, que salieron a la venta por precios por partido que incluso alcanzaban los 700 euros, y esta temporada, con una baja de ingresos considerable al no tener participación en Europa, la entidad ha ido a por las localidades de cortesía: los directivos ya no tendrán invitaciones, en una medida propuesta por el presidente Uriarte, y la intención es que tampoco las tengan los jugadores, que están pendientes de una reunión en la que casi con seguridad salvarán alguna localidad. A los que ya han comunicado que dejarán de recibir invitaciones es a los expresidentes mientras que el club visitante en San Mamés tendrá el cupo mínimo que exige la Liga. El nuevo régimen no tiene mucha explicación para Fernando García Macua, uno de los expresidentes del Athletic. El abogado, entrevistado en COPE Bilbao, ha sido claro en su reflexión. “¿Depende la supervivencia del club de 20 entradas para expresidentes?”, comentó. García Macua dijo que “si el Athletic ha llegado a ser lo que es el por el esfuerzo y aportaciones de muchas personas en muchos papeles de la historia del club. Entre ellos los presidentes, que en un momento determinado y gratis et amore dieron un paso adelante e hicieron un esfuerzo. Muy mal tiene que estar el Athletic si hay que quitar la única atención que desde el primer día se ha tenido con los expresidentes. Si es por la supervivencia del Athletic no diré nada, pero si no es por ello tendré que hacer esta reflexión”. El que fuera presidente del club entre 2007 y 2011 extendió su comentario y añadio que “en mi tiempo el campo era pequeño y las cuentas difíciles de cuadrar. En todos los años ha habido esfuerzos de expresidentes. Ahora tenemos mejor campo que nunca y prácticamente todos los expresidentes vivos participamos en bosquejos, ideas y la ejecución del campo. Desde luego que si fuera por la supervivencia del Athletic esas entradas quedarían encima de la mesa, pero….Es una decisión difícilmente comprensible. Se trata de la institucionalidad del club. Si los presidentes recibieran retribución o prebenda...pero no hay nada de ello. Entre todos hemos sabido mantener la esencia del club como sociedad deportiva. Y el único reconocimento histórico ha sido ese”. García Macua también fue cuestionado respecto a la temporada recién estrenada con Terzic, un técnico alemán sin pasado alguno en la Liga. “Implica un pelín de riesgo, pero soy de los que dice que en el Athletic cada ciertos años necesitamos que haya alguien de fuera. Alguien que no conozca quién le abre la puerta y no le pregunte por sus padres, por los hijos, por cómo ha ido el verano. Y con eso quiero ejemplificar en toda la estructura del club para que el que venga no tenga ideas preconcebidas. Pero también que venga enseñado y aprendido para gestionar algo tan peculiar como el Athletic”.
